summary: El Tehuelche Airport (PMY) is a regional airport serving Puerto Madryn, the gateway city to the Valdés Peninsula on Argentina's Patagonian coast. The airport is named in reference to the Tehuelche indigenous people of the region. It primarily handles domestic flights connecting this remote Patagonian destination to Buenos Aires and other Argentine cities, serving as a key access point for ecotourism and whale-watching expeditions along the Atlantic coast.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of El Tehuelche Airport?
A: The airport serves as the main access point for travelers visiting Puerto Madryn and the Valdés Peninsula, a UNESCO World Heritage site renowned for whale watching and marine wildlife.

Q: Which airlines operate at this airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Argentine domestic carriers offering flights to and from Buenos Aires.

Q: How far is the airport from Puerto Madryn city center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from downtown Puerto Madryn, making transfers quick and convenient.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: No, El Tehuelche is a domestic-only airport; international travelers typically connect through Buenos Aires.
transport_tips: The airport is located approximately 7 kilometers from central Puerto Madryn, and taxis and remis (private hire cars) are typically available to meet arriving flights. Rental car agencies operate in the area and can be arranged in advance for trips along the coast or to the Valdés Peninsula. Pre-booking transport is recommended during peak tourist season (June to December) when whale watching is at its best.
local_tip: If visiting between June and mid-December, consider scheduling your flight for an early arrival—this aligns with prime Southern Right Whale watching season and gives you a full day to join a Peninsula Valdés excursion.
